mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: unsupported pickup: in_container: icebox age handling

summary: The first mismatch at step 72 is Icebox insertion: the JavaScript in_container() guard throws before freeinv() and the C age/timer updates. C later removes the stored corpse at step 82 through out_container() and removed_from_icebox(), but that is a separate continuation gap. The actionable first owner is the whole pickup.c in_container() function; A83 has reservations on naming helpers and welded() used by other in_container() branches.

source.branch: in_container() has passed its early item checks and called freeinv(obj); gc.current_container is an ICE_BOX and age_is_relative(obj) is false. It stores relative age, cancels corpse rot/revive timers, clears mcan for a stored ice troll with OMONST data, or cancels a timed glob shrink timer.
dependencies: include/obj.h:age_is_relative macro; its Boolean controls the age conversion branch.
invent.c:freeinv; C removes the item from inventory before converting its age.
hack.c:obj_to_any and timeout.c:stop_timer; the two stop_timer return values are explicitly discarded, while timer removal mutates the object and timer queue.
include/obj.h:has_omonst and OMONST macros; the predicate guards mutation of the cancelled ice troll traits.

objnam.c:xname, xname_flags, the and related naming helpers; A83 source reservations cover these names used by other in_container() message branches. Do not treat the reservation as source completion.
wield.c:welded; A83 reserves this predicate for the wielded-item branch. Current js/pickup.js still stops at weldmsg when it is true.
obj_is_burning() and snuff_lit() at pickup.c:2626-2627; current JS retains a fail-closed guard for burning objects.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/pickup.c:2558-2710 defines the whole in_container() source unit. At :2624-2657, C calls freeinv(obj) before testing Icebox && !age_is_relative(obj); it stores svm.moves - obj->age, stops ROT_CORPSE and REVIVE_MON timers for a timed corpse, clears mcan on an ice troll corpse with has_omonst(obj), or stops SHRINK_GLOB for a timed glob. The return values from stop_timer() are explicitly discarded.

At examined HEAD b5bb23ff11504c300f032b10b1e17c99b06fc97e, js/pickup.js:2920-2936 checks Icebox and throws before freeinv(obj). This accounts for the step-72 stop; the saved C63 packet .cache/worker-state-loop-20260925.json.deliveries/0630c68d2c093a7132ff6e9db12a5983515863647fd63c01b43348089db91eaf.json independently records step 72 as insertion of an ice-troll corpse.

C caller sites are pickup.c:3174-3184 in use_container(), :3350 and :3376 in menu_loot(), and :3239-3248 in traditional_loot(), which passes in_container() to askchain(). The JavaScript caller sites are pickup.js:2276-2279, :3239, and :3271-3275; whole-function scope should keep these paths wired to the same in_container() implementation.

The removal observed later in the same recording is a distinct C path: pickup.c:2727-2776 out_container() calls removed_from_icebox() at :2758-2759, and :2781-2798 restores absolute age and calls start_corpse_timeout() for a corpse. At current HEAD, js/pickup.js:3087-3094 does not call a removal helper. The C63 packet and normalized trace identify this at step 82, after the step-72 insertion mismatch; it is not the owner of the first divergence.

The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261003003219-v20.json records 72 of 83 screens and 2,902 of 2,920 RNG calls matched. The queue records 11 remaining screens and the step-72 unsupported Icebox age-handling stop. The same packet records a byte-identical independent C replay with run-9WF5zn and recording SHA-256 308480fc042d2387604ee76f5b523fa732739edfd304bfcb78b71814c5d20568.

A83 reservation context in .cache/A83-mnearto-108-scope-event.json and .cache/A83-cmd-ice-scope-event.json names objnam.c:xname, objnam.c:xname_flags, objnam.c:the and related objnam helpers, plus wield.c:welded. These are dependencies of other in_container() branches; the current investigation records the reservation only and does not assert those functions are complete.
